question:
Which of the following statements is correct with reference to the Act passed by the British Parliament in 1858?

I. The Governor-General of India was given the title of Viceroy.

II. The British decided to respect the customary religious and social practices of the people in India.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3 (Both I and II)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The Act of 1858:** The Government of India Act of 1858 was passed by the British Parliament after the Revolt of 1857. It marked the transfer of governance from the East India Company to the British Crown.
 
• **Statement I:** The title of "Governor-General" was replaced with "Viceroy" under this Act. The first Viceroy of India was **Lord Canning**. This title indicated that the Viceroy was the direct representative of the British Crown. ***Hence, Statement I is correct.***
 
• **Statement II:** The Act also emphasized the British Crown's commitment to respecting the **customary religious and social practices** of Indians. This was an attempt to pacify the Indian population after the Revolt of 1857. The British assured Indians that their religious and social traditions would not be interfered with. ***Hence, Statement II is correct.***
